=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py:render_superseded_comment | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The recovery path the comment describes does not work. The superseded step runs before the `/answer` claim. After a person reopens the issue and re-labels it, the labels and body still satisfy `is_candidate` and `resolve_source`.
  WHY: The step finds the pipeline login's existing `ai:plan-superseded:v1` marker, so it posts no new comment. It still sets `SKIP_PLAN=true`, re-applies `ai:closed`, removes `ai:planning` and closes the issue as not planned. A maintainer who follows the comment text gets the issue re-closed with no new explanation. Only `PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR_CHECK_ENABLED=false` actually overrides it, and that is the last sentence of the comment. The last autofix commit added the `ai:planning` instruction, so the misleading text is new in LAST RUN DIFF.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:step "Close superseded CI-repair issue (merged PR)", `merged_check_not_passed` branch, `git checkout --quiet -B "${base_ref}" FETCH_HEAD`, and its new `else` branch | severity=high | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: In this repository the earlier "Stage workflow support files" step does `install -m ... "scripts/${f}"` and `install ... prompts/...` over tracked files. The checkout starts on the PR's former head branch, and the reroute then switches to the base branch. If any staged support file differs between those two commits, git refuses the checkout because it would overwrite local modifications. That is the checkout this change relies on. The new `else` branch now turns that refusal into a skipped planning run, and the new test uses a clean clone with no staged files.
  WHY: In coding-workflows, a merged-but-red CI-repair issue whose former head differs from the base in a staged helper path would fail the reroute on every attempt. The issue would stay in `ai:planning` with planning skipped each run. Skipping is the safe direction, since it avoids planning on the former head, but the issue can stall until the poller's recovery limits are reached. This depends on which paths differ between head and base, so I could not confirm it from the diff alone.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:reroute-failure branch | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The branch deliberately leaves the issue for stall recovery to retry, but sends a WARNING each time. A persistent checkout failure produces one WARNING per retry.
  WHY: WARNING is reserved for conditions a person must act on. This path is auto-retried, which is the DEBUG level in the `tg_helpers.sh` convention. Repeated WARNINGs are noise unless the failure is permanent, in which case a once-per-condition alert would fit better.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py:render_superseded_comment (line 327 area; "If this is wrong, reopen the issue, replace the `ai:closed` label with `ai:planning`, and reply with `/answer`.") | severity=high | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The user-facing recovery recipe is misleading. `is_candidate` returns True based on either the `ai:check-triage` label OR a body re-issue reference (scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py:135-140). Replacing `ai:closed` with `ai:planning` does not change the body, so the next `/answer` re-triggers the superseded check. The check finds the PR still merged and the named check still passing, posts no new comment because the dedup marker already exists, but still writes `SKIP_PLAN=true`, removes `ai:planning`, adds `ai:closed`, and closes the issue again. The user is left believing the override worked while the loop continues.
  WHY: a human operator following the recipe (reopen → swap label → /answer) will see the issue re-closed within the same workflow run. Only the kill switch `PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR_CHECK_ENABLED=false` actually unblocks them, which the comment mentions but the recipe's label-replacement step suggests is unnecessary.
- .github/workflows/plan.yml:branch `merged_check_not_passed` else-arm (the new `tg_send_tracked … "WARNING"` call introduced in the last run); .github/workflows/plan.yml around line 967-973 | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The failed-reroute alert uses WARNING, but the repo convention in agents.md "Telegram alert levels (human-only paging)" reserves WARNING for conditions that require a person to act: "DEBUG means the pipeline is already handling the event (dispatch, retry, re-issue, stall-recovery step, auto-answer, success ping)." This branch is pipeline-handled — it writes `SKIP_PLAN=true`, leaves the issue in its current phase, and relies on stall recovery to retry. Precedent for one-per-condition alerts on auto-retried failures exists (`_standalone_conflict_count_attempt` sends one WARNING only after `STANDALONE_CONFLICT_STUCK_ALERT_ATTEMPTS`, default 3) and for pipeline-handled conditions to use DEBUG (the parallel "Closed superseded CI-repair issue" success path on the same step already uses DEBUG).
  WHY: each plan.yml run that hits the same persistent reroute failure (for example, a checkout blocked by locally modified tracked support files, which the cross-pollination summary flagged) will re-emit a WARNING. That violates the convention and turns a stall-recovery step into repeated human paging, which is what DEBUG exists to prevent.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_7-plus ===
- scripts/plan_superseded_merged_pr.py:render_superseded_comment, lines 327-328 | severity=high | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The recovery instructions tell users to "reopen the issue, replace the `ai:closed` label with `ai:planning`, and reply with `/answer`", but this does not work. When the issue is reopened with `ai:planning` and the user replies `/answer`, the workflow runs the superseded check again. The marker `<!-- ai:plan-superseded:v1 pr=... head=... -->` is still present from the pipeline login, so the comment is skipped (deduplication), but `SKIP_PLAN=true` is still set, the `ai:closed` label is reapplied, and the issue is closed again as "not planned". The underlying conditions (merged PR with passing checks) have not changed, so the workflow will keep closing the issue on every retry.
  WHY: The marker-based deduplication only skips the comment post, not the close. The classifier still returns `superseded` because the PR is merged and the check passed. The user's label replacement is overwritten. The only way to prevent re-closing is to set `PLAN_SUPERSEDED_MERGED_PR_CHECK_ENABLED=false`, but the recovery instructions mention this only as a secondary option at the end, after the primary (non-working) recovery path.
